reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it documents troubleshooting a Samsung television and attempting to access its service menu, including a remote-control demonstration and discussion of an incorrect replacement board. The speaker tests a service-menu code and warns that changing settings can damage the configuration, presenting technical guidance and uncertainty. Requests to subscribe or share are ordinary audience engagement and are not described as conditions for payment, credentials, investment, or another financial offer.

opening.argument: Judge, the repair lesson is not the only invitation here. The description pairs an action with a potential reward: follow the creator on Instagram for tech videos and giveaways. It also directs viewers to subscribe for more videos. That pairing makes the giveaway a reason to enter the creator's external audience funnel, even though the video supplies no giveaway terms or evidence that following produces a reward.

citations.quote: * Follow Tampatec on Instagram for tech videos and giveaways https://www.instagram.com/tampatec/
Learn more about Tech and how to fix electronics, Subscribe to Tampatec here- https://www.youtube.com/tampatec

rebuttal.rebuttal: The service-menu demonstration and its warning can be genuine without accounting for every viewer solicitation. The defense treats subscription as ordinary engagement, but the description goes further: it associates following an external account with giveaways. The repair discussion does not establish what those giveaways are or whether viewers can actually obtain them.

citations.quote: * Follow Tampatec on Instagram for tech videos and giveaways https://www.instagram.com/tampatec/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The description says the account has videos and giveaways; it does not promise a reward for following, set out a claim process, or require an action to receive anything. The video itself reports a failed service-menu attempt and an unresolved TV fault. An unspecified giveaway mention does not turn that repair account into a deceptive reward offer.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals together. The description offers giveaways through an external social account, lists several shopping links that support the channel, and says some products are received free for guides or reviews. The video also asks viewers to share and subscribe. This combination gives the creator several ways to move viewers from a troubleshooting video into promotional channels. The record does not provide giveaway rules or verify any reward, so the reward language deserves scrutiny rather than being dismissed as incidental.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the presenter warns about service-menu settings. That warning does not resolve the separate promotional signals in the description. Nor does the absence of a stated payment or credential request establish that the giveaway invitation is reliable; the supplied material leaves its terms unstated.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those signals do not establish deception. The description openly says the shopping links support the channel and discloses that some review products are received free. It does not tie a purchase, subscription, or follow to a guaranteed giveaway reward. The recorded troubleshooting remains specific and unresolved, rather than a demonstrated reward-claim flow.

opening.argument: Judge, the instructional setting also carries promotion. The presenter names a parts seller and praises its customer service while discussing the board, and the description opens with places to buy TV parts. It then sends viewers to an Instagram account associated with giveaways. Repair advice builds a reason to trust and follow the creator; the giveaway supplies an additional incentive to take that step. The promotional role matters even if the television fault shown here is real.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes the attempted service-menu entry, but that demonstration does not negate the invitations surrounding it. The seller praise and parts links are placed alongside a follow request tied to giveaways. The question is whether the educational presentation also steers viewers toward a reward-oriented promotional channel; the description shows that it does.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Mentioning parts suppliers fits the documented repair: the presenter says the seller sent the wrong board and issued a return label. The Instagram line mentions giveaways but gives no specific reward, eligibility condition, or claim instruction. Promotion around an instructional video is not, by itself, evidence of a deceptive reward solicitation.
